steps.text: Combine lentils, carrots, onion, garlic, bay leaf, and thyme in a saucepan. Add enough water to cover by 1 inch; bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes or until lentils are tender but not mushy.
Drain lentils and vegetables and remove bay leaf. Add olive oil, lemon juice, celery, parsley, salt and pepper. Toss gently to mix and serve at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Mediterranean Lentil Salad
raw_recipe.description: This lentil salad made with tender brown lentils, carrots, red onion, celery, and a fresh lemon dressing is a delicious and nutritious salad.
raw_recipe.name: Mediterranean Lentil Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Combine lentils, carrots, onion, garlic, bay leaf, and thyme in a saucepan. Add enough water to cover by 1 inch; bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes or until lentils are tender but not mushy.
Drain lentils and vegetables and remove bay leaf. Add olive oil, lemon juice, celery, parsley, salt and pepper. Toss gently to mix and serve at room temperature.

review.reviewBody: Very yummy recipe. I make it with 16 oz of lentils, triple the other ingredients, and I add about 3T cumin, 1T curry to the lentils as they cook. I find the lentils take about 35-40 min to cook. It is a fabulous recipe to make in advance, and lasts quite a while. One of my family's favorites - thanks!

This was so delicious. You must use brown lentils because others tend to be too soft. I followed the others and added less sugar (Monk sugar) than the recipe stated. I also cooked the lentil in vegetable broth and curry as others suggested and omitted salt, thyme and bay leaf as suggested. This was so delicious. Next time I will add thawed frozen peas and corn as someone suggested. Thank you for this easy and delicious recipe. The dressing really made this dish.

This is really good. You will likely feel the need for a little more acidity either through additional lemon juice or your favorite vinegar. I added red wine vinegar. I took the suggestions of others- cooking my lentils in chicken broth instead of water, adding cumin to the cooking lentils, keeping the vegetables raw and cutting back the onion to 1/2 cup. Note- As quickly as possible reduce the lentils to a medium simmer. Boiling or fast simmer causes the mushiness some of the other reviewers experienced. Also, one cup of lentils actually requires 2 cups liquid to cook.

I changed a lot for the recipe based on other reviews. For the vegetables I only cooked about half and left the other half raw, soaking in lemon juice and salt while the lentils cooked. I also added orange and yellow bell peppers and half a habanero pepper. It wasn't too spicy but had just enough kick. Finally, in addition to the parsley, i also chopped up the celery leaves and threw it in with one tomato. I just made it for a potlock and got so many compliments.
Made as written and we liked it a lot. Made again but added 2 tsp of yellow curry powder and it was delicious.
I added extra spices to it & cooked the lentils in veggie broth instead of water. Turned out great.

I made this using all the ingredients as listed, but I didn't cook all the veggies with the lentils. I only cooked the garlic,half of the onion, bay leaf and thyme. The rest was raw, which I think is best for this salad. I tripled the fresh parsley because it needed it. It also needed a lot more lemon, so I added the juice of one whole lemon. I tried it at room temp and it was very good. I'm looking forward to trying it tomorrow once the flavors meld.

Makes a good base recipe, although it needs some extra seasonings. I've made it several times, but typically I double the celery, onion , and garlic. I prefer lime juice over lemon juice. I also increase the parsley, and have added in fresh thyme and spearmint as well.

This was just okay for me, but I'm rating four stars, instead of three, as part of the reason I wasn't crazy about this is just personal preference: too many lentils = ) ...yes, I get the irony...a lentil salad with too many lentils. I choose this salad as a change from bean salads because of the nutritional values (protein; fiber; ETC). Next time I would use half as many lentils, and add more flavor to the dressing. I actually removed a bunch of lentils from the salad and froze them to use in another batch later. I love carrots...so I will likely end up making a carrot salad with lentils!!!

Pretty easy recipe. Tried it as is then freestyled :-) It's tasty as it is (great side dish) but it also lends itself well to variations. I doubled the carrots which I added in the last 5mins of lentil cook time (13-15 mins or else it'll go too mushy). Doubled the celery as well. I added corn kernels and toasted pumpkin seeds to add texture. I add chopped cucumber (no seeds) just before eating. Used a roasted sesame and paprika salt blend. Best part is it's filling and keeps well.

I personally have been disgusted by lentils for the longest time, (the way their texture mixes with their casings is not appetizing) but this was the best thing I have tasted with lentils. The texture and casings were still bothering me so I decided to make this into a dip/salsa by blending it in the food processor.

I did make a few changes, by adding the diced tomatoes and used light Italian dressing instead of oil, then experimented with Chipotle powder, cumin and paprika, to give it more flavor and added more salt and pepper (blending it beforehand seemed to muddle the flavors). It turns out to be a very refreshing dip!
Easy to make. I add more lemon. Recipe said serve warm. We found it taster cold. Try both and you decide

Weird to cook the red onion, which should always be eaten raw. Next time I won’t cook any of the vegetables. I did add cumin and curry as suggested by others. Also some fresh scallions. I think I’ll add fresh radishes and peas too.

I needed cooked lentils for a salad so chose this quick recipe without added Indian spices, which I love. I added garlic salt and onion powder but it still lacked flavor. I am going to add lemon juice before serving the salad.
It was missing something......
Added cumin. 👍🏼
Followed recipe and found this to be to bland for me.
Easy to make and great flavors.

Absolutely delicious! Used half the recommended amount in thyme and used all dried instead of fresh herbs and it still came out amazing! Not sure how many servings it’s suppose to make but I think I’m eating half lol
Very tasty. Just make sure you don’t overlook the lentils. Made a batch for the week and it kept well.
